news.headline: NASA Wants to Give the Hubble Telescope a Boost
news.body: The Hubble Space Telescope has been taking amazing pictures of space for more than 35 years! But Hubble is slowly sinking lower as it circles Earth, and it has no engine of its own to climb back up. Now NASA is asking companies for ideas, like sending a spacecraft to push Hubble higher or even fix it up. Scientists say that could help Hubble keep making new discoveries for many more years.

news.headline: Scientists Meet a Brand-New Kind of Wild Cat
news.body: Scientists have found a whole new species of wild cat living in the forests of Bolivia, in South America. It's called the tilcayo, the name local people have used for it for a very long time. The little spotted cat looks a lot like other small wild cats, but it has bigger, wigglier spots, shorter fur and a longer, less bushy tail. Figuring out it was truly new took almost 10 years of detective work!

news.headline: Meet the First Known Fruit-Eating Dinosaur
news.body: Scientists have named a new dinosaur called Infernogallus. It was a small, beaked dinosaur that lived at the same time as T. rex and Triceratops. By scanning its skull, scientists found chewing muscles like the ones fruit-eating parrots have today. That means it could slide its beak back and forth to mash up soft fruit. It's the first dinosaur known to have been built for eating fruit!
